subject.title: Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District — Measure N (School Bonds)

text: To maintain quality academic facilities at Los Gatos High School and Saratoga High School by replacing leaky roofs and failing restrooms, plumbing, electrical, heating/cooling systems; improving school safety; updating, repairing and equipping schools including science, technology, engineering, arts, math, robotics, and career/college readiness classrooms/labs; shall Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District's measure be adopted, authorizing $321,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying approximately $30 per $100,000 assessed value ($23,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with oversight, annual audits, and local control?
A "yes" vote is a vote to authorize the issuance and sale of up to $321 million of general obligation bonds to fund school facilities projects as described in the Measure.
A "no" vote is a vote not to authorize the issuance and sale of the bonds.

California law permits school districts to issue bonds with the approval of 55% of district voters. Such bonds may be used only for construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, or replacement of school facilities, including furnishing and equipping those facilities, or the acquisition or lease of real property for school facilities.
The Board of Trustees (Board) of the Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District (District) has placed on the ballot a Measure authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $321 million in such bonds.
As identified in the Measure, projects may include but are not limited to:
Replacing leaky roofs;
Improving school safety with campus security and emergency communications systems;
Updating, repairing, and equipping science technology, engineering, arts, math classrooms and labs;
Providing up-to-date instructional tools for teachers;
Replacing and repairing failing plumbing, electrical, heating, and cooling systems;
Improving accessibility for students with disabilities;
Updating and upgrading failing school restrooms;
Updating athletic facilities for school and community use;
Upgrading and modernizing robotics labs and maker spaces for hands-on learning;
Making energy-efficiency upgrades;
Upgrading or replacing school support facilities including physical education, music, and art classrooms, wood and metal shops, and libraries;
Removing hazardous materials like asbestos, mold, and lead paint; and
Resurfacing or replacing asphalt, fields, and downspout drainage systems.

Bond proceeds may be spent on eligible project costs, such as acquiring equipment and paying for environmental studies, assessment reviews, and design and construction documentation, as well as engineering, legal, project management, and training costs and expenses. In accordance with state law, the Measure states that bond proceeds would not be used for teacher or school administrator salaries or other operating expenses.

These general obligation bonds will be payable from ad valorem taxes levied on taxable real property within the District. The Measure states that the best estimate of the average annual tax rate to be levied to repay the proposed bonds is $30.00 per $100,000 of assessed value, that the final fiscal year in which the tax is anticipated to be collected will be 2056-2057, and that the best estimate of the total debt service during the life of the bond, including principal and interest, is $690 million.

State law requires the District to take certain steps to account for the bond proceeds. Accordingly, the District has listed in the Measure the specific projects to be funded, including a certification that, in developing the list, the Board evaluated safety, class size reduction, and information technology needs. Additionally, the District will appoint a citizens' oversight committee, conduct annual independent audits, create an account into which proceeds shall be deposited, and comply with state law reporting requirements.

Tony LoPresti
County Counsel

By: /s/ Nick DeFiesta
Deputy County Counsel
Tax Rate Statement
TAX RATE STATEMENT CONCERNING MEASURE

An election will be held in the Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District (the "District") on November 3, 2026 to authorize the sale of up to $321,000,000 in general obligation bonds. If such bonds are authorized and sold, principal and interest on the bonds will be payable only from the proceeds of

tax levies made upon the taxable property in the District. The following information is submitted in compliance with Sections 9400-9406 of the Elections Code of the State of California. Such information is based upon the best estimates and projections presently available from official sources, upon experience within the District, and other demonstrable factors.
The following information is provided pursuant to Elections Code Section 9401:

1. The best estimate of the average annual tax rate that would be required to be levied to fund this bond issue over the entire duration of the bond debt service, based on estimated assessed valuations available at the time of filing of this statement, is $30.00 per $100,000 (3.0¢ per $100) of assessed valuation. It is currently expected that the tax will be collected until fiscal year 2056-57.

2. The best estimate of the highest tax rate that would be required to be levied to fund this bond issue, for each year that bonds are outstanding, based on estimated assessed valuations available at the time of filing this statement, is $30.00 per $100,000 (3.0¢ per $100) of assessed valuation, which is projected to be the same in every fiscal year the bonds remain outstanding.
3. The best estimate of total debt service, including principal and interest, that would be required to be repaid if all the bonds are issued and sold will be approximately $690 million.

Voters should note that these estimates are based on projections derived from information obtained from official sources, and are based on the assessed value (not market value) of taxable property on the County's official tax rolls. Property owners should consult their own property tax bills and tax advisors to determine their property's assessed value and any applicable tax exemptions.

The attention of all voters is directed to the fact that the foregoing information is based upon projections and estimates only, which amounts are not maximum amounts and durations and are not binding upon the District. The actual debt service, tax rates and the years in which they will apply may vary depending on the timing of bond sales, the par amount of bonds sold at each sale and actual increases in assessed valuations. The timing of the bond sales and the amount of bonds sold at any given time will be determined by the District based on the need for project funds and other considerations. Actual assessed valuations will depend upon the amount and value of taxable property within the District as determined by the County Assessor in the annual assessment and the equalization process.

/s/ Heath Rocha
Superintendent
Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District
EXHIBIT B

FULL TEXT BALLOT PROPOSITION
OF THE LOS GATOS-SARATOGA UNION HIGH SCHOOL DISTRICT
BOND MEASURE ELECTION NOVEMBER 3, 2026
The following is the full proposition presented to the voters by the Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District.

"To maintain quality academic facilities at Los Gatos High School and Saratoga High School by replacing leaky roofs and failing restrooms, plumbing, electrical, heating/cooling systems; improving school safety; updating, repairing and equipping schools including science, technology, engineering, arts, math, robotics, and career/college readiness classrooms/labs; shall Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District's measure be adopted, authorizing $321,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying approximately $30 per $100,000 assessed value ($23,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with oversight, annual audits, and local control?"
PROJECT LIST
The Board of Trustees of the Los Gatos-Saratoga Union High School District is committed to

strong: maintaining high qualify academics and programs

text: at Los Gatos High School and Saratoga High School by

strong: repairing and upgrading aging school facilities

text: and providing safe, secure, modern classrooms, labs and technology needed to support high quality instruction in

strong: math, science, engineering, technology
and other skilled trades

text: . To that end, the Board evaluated the District's

strong: urgent and critical facility needs

text: , including safety issues, class size reduction, basic repairs, computer and information technology in developing the types of projects to be funded by this measure as described below.
In approving this Project List, the Board of Trustees determines that the District

strong: must:
(i) Replace leaky roofs and improve school safety; and
(ii) Provide up-to-date instructional tools for teachers; and
(iii) Replace failing plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling systems; and
(iv) Adhere to specific fiscal accountability safeguards such as:
(a) Every penny must be spent on local high schools and cannot be spent on administrator salaries;
(b) Prohibit the State from taking any of the funds raised;
(c) Require annual independent financial and performance audits; and
(d) Require the review of all expenditures by an independent citizens' oversight committee and public disclosure of all spending.

text: The Project List includes the following types of upgrades and improvements at District high schools, facilities and sites:
LOCALLY CONTROLLED FUNDING FOR SCHOOL IMPROVEMENTS
School Repair, Safety and Upgrade Projects

strong: Goals and Purposes:

Some high school buildings are over 100 years old. Long-term, it costs more to maintain currently plumbing and energy systems that are well beyond their useful life than to replace them. This measure will replace aging school roofs, windows, plumbing, HVAC and energy systems to avoid costly ongoing repairs. Investing in local school benefits all members of the community whether or not you have school-age children by maintaining high property values.
Improve school safety and campus security systems

text: including security fencing, security cameras, and emergency communications systems
Upgrade electrical and technology systems and wiring

strong: Replace leaky roofs

text: Improve school accessibility for students with disabilities

strong: Update and upgrade failing school restrooms

text: Improve student safety at school pick up and drop off areas
Update athletic facilities for school and community use.
SUPPORT HIGH QUALITY INSTRUCTION IN MATH, SCIENCE, ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY
Projects That Improve Student Success

strong: Goals and Purposes:

While our students, teachers and academic programs are among the best in the nation, our high school buildings are in desperate need of repairs and updates. This measure will bring classrooms and labs up to the standard necessary to maintain our prestigious academics.

Maintaining our high schools as the best in the State depends on attracting and retaining our high-quality teachers and staff. This measure will make sure our classrooms and technology are up-to-date so that top teacher will want to continuing teaching here.
Update, repair and equip science, technology, engineering, arts, math classrooms and labs to support high quality instruction
Replace and repair failing plumbing, electrical, heating and cooling systems

text: Keep computer systems and instructional technology up-to-date.
Upgrade and modernize robotics labs and maker spaces for hands-on learning
FISCAL ACCOUNTABILITY

strong: This Measure requires a clear system of accountability, including a citizen's oversight committee to ensure all funds are spent properly. By law, every penny of this Measure must be spent on our local high schools and no funds can be taken by the state.

text: In accordance with Education Code Section 15272, the Board of Trustees will appoint a

strong: citizens' oversight committee

text: and

strong: conduct annual independent audits

text: to ensure that funds are spent only on District projects and for no other purpose. The expenditure of bond money on these projects is subject to stringent financial accountability requirements. By law, performance and financial audits will be performed annually, and all bond expenditures will be monitored by an independent citizens' oversight committee to ensure that funds are spent as promised and specified. The citizens' oversight committee must include, among others, representation of a bona fide taxpayers association, a business organization and a senior citizens organization. No District employees or vendors are allowed to serve on the citizens' oversight committee.

strong: No Administrator Salaries:

text: Proceeds from the sale of the bonds authorized by this proposition shall be used only for the acquisition, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, or replacement of school facilities, including the furnishing and equipping of school facilities, and not for any other purpose, including teacher and school administrator salaries and other operating expenses.

In addition to the projects listed above, the repair and renovation of each of the existing school and District support facilities may include, but not be limited to, some or all of the following: add or renovate student and staff restrooms; repair, replace and upgrade electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems; upgrade of facilities for energy efficiencies, electrical generation and financial savings, including photovoltaic/solar installations and battery energy storage; improve accessibility for students, staff and the public with disabilities; repair, upgrade, and replace worn-out and deteriorated roofs, gutters, windows, walls, tackboards, floors, sinks, doors and drinking fountains/hydration stations; construct or renovate offices and facilities for multipurpose and indoor/outdoor learning spaces, more efficient areas for professional development and administration and for the safety of students on campuses; install wiring and electrical systems to safely accommodate computers, technology and other electrical devices; upgrade, replace or construct support facilities including central plants, boilers, administrative, college and career counseling, central kitchens, physical education, music, art, and performing and fine arts classrooms or facilities, wood and metal shops, science, robotics, STEM/STEAM labs/classrooms, computer labs/classrooms, career technical classrooms and facilities (including graphic design, fashion design and technical drawing), makerspaces, culinary arts facilities, media centers/libraries and buildings, covered eating areas, shade and rain shelter, covered walkways, transportation and maintenance facilities and yards; acquire modular/portable classrooms; repair, upgrade and replace fire and intrusion alarms, emergency communications, public address, speaker, and security systems; including security protections on windows, improve facilities to satisfy ADA and seismic requirements; as needed, removal of hazardous materials like asbestos, mold, and lead paint from older schools, as needed; improve/resurface or replace asphalt, broken concrete and improve hard courts, walkways, turf, tracks, fields (athletic, open and utility/scrimmage), irrigation, and downspout drainage systems and campus landscaping; install and improve signage, wayfinding flagpoles, solar electric systems and fencing; expand parking and improve pick-up and drop-off areas and crosswalks; improve all site utilities; acquire land; construct new school buildings; upgrade or replace interior and exterior painting, floor covering, including carpets, and school facades; demolition; upgrade kitchens, food service and school cafeterias; construct various forms of storage and support spaces and classrooms; improve quads; repair, upgrade and install interior and exterior lighting systems and back-up power generators; improve, construct, or replace athletic fields/stadiums, fieldhouse, concessions, bleachers, lockers/locker rooms, weight rooms, field lighting, gymnasiums, and other facilities to support student health, fitness and safety; construct or upgrade aquatic facilities, pools, including pool filtration systems, plaster and decking; repair, install and replace outdated fences, including security fences and security systems (including access control systems, electronic locks, and cameras), provide lunch shelters, indoor space for assemblies or for rainy day lunch; upgrade and construct music labs, multi-purpose rooms, theatres, learning centers and media centers; add or upgrade parking lots including solar systems and electric vehicle charging stations. In addition to the listed projects stated above, the Project List also includes the acquisition of a variety of instructional, maintenance and operational equipment, including the reduction or retirement of outstanding lease obligations and interim funding incurred to advance fund projects from the Project List; payment of the costs of preparation of all facility planning, facility studies, assessment reviews, facility master plan preparation and updates, environmental studies (including environmental investigation, remediation and monitoring), design and construction documentation, DSA oversight, and temporary housing of dislocated District activities caused by construction projects.

The upgrading of technology infrastructure includes, but is not limited to, network rewiring, cabling, computers, portable interface devices, servers, switches, routers, modules, sound projection systems, laser printers, scanners and copiers, digital white boards and smart boards, document projectors, upgrade voice-over-IP, clock/telephone/intercom systems, call manager and network security/firewall, wireless technology systems, refresh classroom technology, miscellaneous IT and instructional equipment, data storage, archiving and preservation, phones, identity cards and the construction and installation of a data center in the cloud for the District's enterprise systems, such as resource planning, websites, domain name systems, cloud applications and information security.

The budget for each project is an estimate and may be affected by factors beyond the District's control. Some projects throughout the District may be undertaken as joint use projects in cooperation with other local public or non-profit agencies. The final cost of each project will be determined as plans and construction documents are finalized, construction bids are received, construction contracts are awarded and projects are completed. Based on the final costs of each project, certain of the projects described above may be delayed or may not be completed. Demolition of portable classrooms and existing facilities and reconstruction of facilities scheduled for repair and upgrade may occur, if the Board determines that such an approach would be more cost-effective in creating more enhanced and operationally efficient campuses. Necessary site preparation/restoration may occur in connection with new construction, renovation or remodeling, or installation or removal of relocatable or modular classrooms, including ingress and egress, removing, replacing, or installing irrigation or drainage systems, traffic signals, sewer or utility lines, trees and landscaping, relocating fire access roads, road widening, and acquiring any necessary easements, licenses, permits, or rights of way to the property. The listed projects will be completed as needed. Each project is assumed to include its share of furniture, equipment, architectural, engineering, legal fees and similar planning costs, connection fees, program and project management, staff training expenses and a customary contingency for unforeseen design and construction costs. Proceeds of the bonds may be used to pay or reimburse the District for the cost of District bond audits and staff when performing work on or necessary and incidental to bond projects. Bond proceeds shall only be expended for the types of projects and purposes identified herein. The District shall create an account into which proceeds of the bonds shall be deposited and comply with the reporting requirements of Government Code § 53410.

strong: Vote Yes on N to repair our high schools, maintain our excellent reputation, and protect local property values.

text: Los Gatos High School and Saratoga High School are central to our community's identity. Our high schools are among the best in the state and nation and are the #1 driver of local property values. They are why many of us move here and stay.

Yet some high school buildings are between 65, 75, and even 100 years old, and in desperate need of repairs and updates. Roofs leak, plumbing fails and outdated energy systems are inefficient. If we wait, repair costs will go up, and our aging high schools will require even more costly maintenance.

Additionally, many classrooms and labs don't meet the modern standards necessary to maintain our prestigious academics. Award-winning programs like our robotics team are doing more with less, but the need is dire. Upgrading our schools will allow us to continue offering the best academic programs and ensure that the most qualified teachers will want to continue teaching here.
Your YES vote on Measure N will help avoid expensive, temporary fixes, and

strong: help our high schools qualify for millions in state matching funds.
Vote Yes on N to:

text: Repair leaky roofs
Replace failing plumbing, electrical, heating, and cooling systems
Update failing school restrooms
Improve school safety
Provide up-to-date instructional tools for teachers
Upgrade science, technology, arts, math, robotics, and career technical education classrooms and labs

strong: Strict Accountability Keeps Measure N Local:

text: Every penny stays local—nothing can be taken by the State or Federal governments
Annual independent audits and citizens' oversight ensure funds are spent as promised
Measure N can't fund administrator salaries

strong: Essential repairs and upgrades can't wait. Help protect the high-quality education our community expects and our students deserve. Vote Yes on N!

text: Our opponents talk about priorities. Protecting excellent education in safe, modern high schools is our #1 priority. We've been doing it responsibly with as little cost to homeowners as possible—in fact, our District has the lowest tax rate in the county.
Perhaps our opponents haven't been inside our high schools in recent years. The need is real and the time to act is now.
We cannot rely on the State or Federal government to provide the funding our schools need. If we want to keep our high schools among the best in the nation, we need to act locally. We need Measure N.
Our opponents clamor for accountability. Luckily for them, Measure N has strict transparency and oversight requirements!
Every penny stays local—nothing can be taken by the State or Federal government
Annual independent audits and citizens' oversight are mandatory
A detailed project list outlines the use of all funds
Measure N can't fund administrator salaries
Speaking of homes, if your roof was leaking, would you fix it? YES.
If your bathrooms and plumbing were busted, would you replace them? YES.
If your home was 65, 75, or even 100 years old, would it need improvements? YES.
If you lived in a different school district, would your property value be as strong? NO.
We're proud to call Los Gatos and Saratoga home. We know how critical our high schools are to our community identity.

strong: That's why we're voting YES on N—for the next generation of local students!
